part1_theEscapeDefect.defect: `dagPanelKeyAction`'s Escape branch returned `{ consumed: true, pin: false }` UNCONDITIONALLY. The host's plugin-panel dispatcher turns any `preventDefault()` into `consumed = true` (`lib/types/components/sidePanel/pluginPanelAdapter.js`: `preventDefault: () => { consumed = true }`, `return consumed`), and a consumed press never reaches the host's own fallback (`lib/types/components/sidePanel/useSidePanel.js`: `if (key.escape === true) { setFocus('chat'); stop(); return true }`). Opening `/mpd panel` therefore took the keyboard with no keyboard way back.
part1_theEscapeDefect.fix: The keymap now takes the PIN as a fourth argument (`pinned: string | undefined = undefined`) and consumes Escape ONLY while a task is pinned: `return pinned === undefined ? { consumed: false } : { consumed: true, pin: false }`. The page handler passes the same live cell the pin itself uses (`dagPanelKeyAction(bare, order, cursorNow(), pinnedNow())`), so a press delivered in one event-loop turn sees what the previous press asked for. Nothing else in the keymap moved: the arrows, the pin keys and every scroll key keep their consumption rules and their values.
part1_theEscapeDefect.f_a_where: printed from the real function into `f-a-observed.txt`; asserted by two arms in `test/panel-dag.test.ts` (`F-a the keymap's OWN values…`, `F-a ON A MOUNTED PAGE…`), the second of which drives the REAL host listener shape (`{input, key, preventDefault}`) and shows 0 consumptions with no pin, 1 with a pin, and the pin body gone after the release.

partS_theStatusRow.option: (b) MARK — and the choice is forced, not preferred
partS_theStatusRow.why_option_b: NO session id is reachable on that seam, and the host's own signature is the proof. `lib/types/dsh-adapter/status.d.ts` (dsh-tui 0.14.0): `set(key: string, text: string | number | boolean | undefined, identity?: Context): () => void` — a SCALAR, whose trailing `identity` is the plugin's own ctx and 'only feeds the effect ledger's pluginId'; and the rich companion `registerView(descriptor: TuiStatusViewDescriptor, identity?: Context)` where `TuiStatusViewDescriptor.component: React.ComponentType<TuiStatusViewProps>` and `TuiStatusViewProps = { readonly React: typeof React; readonly ui: TuiStatusViewUi }`. The host's own header states it: 'It deliberately receives no input, channel, or raw-terminal capability.' Our `TuiStatusView.render(): string | number | boolean | undefined` takes NO arguments and the adapter hands it nothing (`packages/mpd-tui-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts`), and `registerStatus`'s call site passes only `workspaceRoot`/`home`/readouts (`packages/mpd-tui-plugin/src/index.ts`). The only ambient session source in the composition is `adapter.liveAgents()` — ALL live sessions, which cannot identify the READER (the sidebar page gets its id from `host.snapshot().sessionId`; a status view receives no `host`). So (a) is unprovable here and (b) is the honest behaviour.
partS_theStatusRow.fix: `state.ts :: statusLine` appends the contract vocabulary to the TEAM part when a team is shown: `team OTHERBOARD 1·0/4 (workspace-level)`. Parenthesised and attached to that one part so it reads as a qualifier, never as a counter; `plans`/`workmates`/progress keep their exact meaning and stay unmarked (they are workspace facts by definition). A row that finds NO team is NOT marked — a workspace-level read that resolves nothing means the workspace holds no team at all, so there is nothing that could belong to another session. Reusing `WORKSPACE_SCOPE_MARKER` (`team-state.ts`) keeps ONE token across surfaces.

honestBounds: The pre-fix behaviour of the STATUS ROW is quoted from the previous lane's capture, not re-captured here: my single PTY boot runs the FIXED dist, so it can witness the post-fix frame only. The pre-fix frame is cited verbatim and is on disk.

The status row cannot be SCOPED, only MARKED: the seam hands no host and no channel (host `TuiStatusViewProps {React, ui}`). A reader who wants this session's board must look at the panel, which IS scoped and says `no team in this session` when that is the truth.

`(workspace-level)` therefore appears on the status row whenever the workspace holds a team, including in a frame whose panel body is in state 2 — the row is honestly describing ITS OWN read (a workspace-level summary), not claiming a state. A frame scan that wants to classify the PANEL must key on the panel's body rows; the token is orthogonal inside each surface, not across two surfaces with different scopes.

The `Ctrl+A` contact is inert on dsh-tui 0.13.0+ by the version gate, so its marked read was evidenced at the code level (an arm over `readDashboardWorkflow` + `teamWorkflowLines`), not on a PTY: no PTY can reach it on this host.

The real-PTY run's first attempt (08:42) reported a FALSE FAIL because its marker (`task dependency graph`) only exists on a board-drawing scene; this session has no team of its own, so the scene it correctly opened renders the session-empty state. The marker was corrected and the arm re-run; BOTH runs and both log sections stay in the evidence directory, and no assertion rests on attempt 1. (This box's `date` is uutils coreutils 0.10.0, whose `%3N` is not offset by the fractional second — no latency claim is made here, so no timing depends on it; the log uses whole-second UTC stamps only.)
Test count moved 443 -> 447 (four new arms: two keymap arms, one no-team status arm, one real-seam status arm); the dashboard-key and session-scope arms were EXTENDED/INVERTED, never deleted.

No latency or throughput claim is made by this lane: the PTY evidence is a behavioural walk, and every frame's timestamp is the capture instant tmux recorded (whole-second UTC, written next to the frame as `<name>.at`).
